why: src/tools/configHelper/handler.ts passes the caller's configFile string only as the `config` field of a JSON POST to CircleCI's own config-validate API (src/clients/circleci/configValidate.ts); it is never parsed, executed, templated, or written to disk locally, so there is no local sink for the argument.

outputDir flows through resolveSafeOutputDir/joinWithinDir/safeWriteFileSync in src/lib/usage-api/getUsageApiData.ts and src/lib/file-output/safePaths.ts, which canonicalizes symlinks with realpathBestEffort, blocks system directories and hidden/node_modules/launch-agent path segments, restricts writes to cwd/home/tmp (or an operator-set MCP_FILE_OUTPUT_ROOTS), and opens the destination file with O_NOFOLLOW to defeat a symlink-swap race; the only fetch() call in this path targets download_urls returned by CircleCI's own usage-export job-status response, not a caller-supplied URL.

projectSlug/projectURL/workspaceRoot+gitRemoteURL in src/tools/getFlakyTests/handler.ts only select which CircleCI insights/tests API endpoints are queried; the optional local file-write branch (writeTestsToFiles) writes under a directory built solely from the server-configured FILE_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY env var (never caller input) using filenames produced by generateSafeFilename, which strips test.name to [A-Za-z0-9_-] before use, so no caller-controlled path reaches fs.writeFileSync.

src/lib/usage-api/findUnderusedResourceClasses.ts readAndParseCSV calls resolveSafeInputFile(csvFilePath) (src/lib/file-output/safePaths.ts) before fs.readFileSync, which resolves symlinks and rejects any path outside cwd/home/tmp or landing on a system directory / hidden / node_modules segment, so a caller cannot read /etc/passwd, ~/.ssh, or similar outside the allowed roots.

formatJobLogs in src/lib/pipeline-job-logs/getJobLogs.ts validates outputDir with the same resolveSafeOutputDir + joinWithinDir + safeWriteFileSync(O_NOFOLLOW) guard used by download_usage_api_data before writing the log file; projectSlug/branch/projectURL/workspaceRoot+gitRemoteURL are only used to select CircleCI API calls via project-detection/index.ts, which does pure string parsing (no shell, no fs access).

src/tools/getJobTestResults/handler.ts forwards projectSlug/branch/jobNumber/pipelineNumber (derived via pure string parsing in project-detection/index.ts) to circleci.tests.getJobTests, i.e. CircleCI's own test-metadata API scoped to the caller's own token; there is no local file, shell, or eval sink.

src/tools/getLatestPipelineStatus/handler.ts only uses projectSlug/branch/projectURL/workspaceRoot+gitRemoteURL to look up pipeline status through CircleCI's own API (getLatestPipelineWorkflows); no local sink exists for any of the arguments.

src/tools/listArtifacts/handler.ts uses projectSlug/branch/projectURL/workspaceRoot+gitRemoteURL only to call CircleCI's pipelines/workflows/jobs APIs and list job artifacts; artifact URLs returned by CircleCI are echoed back as text, never fetched or written locally by this tool.

src/tools/listComponentVersions/handler.ts forwards projectSlug/projectID/orgID/componentID/environmentID verbatim to CircleCI's own deploys API (fetchEnvironments/fetchProjectComponents/fetchComponentVersions); results are only ever formatted into text, with no local file/shell/eval sink.

src/tools/listFollowedProjects/inputSchema.ts declares `z.object({})` — the tool accepts no caller-controlled arguments at all; the handler just calls circleciPrivate.me.getFollowedProjects() and formats the response.

src/tools/rerunWorkflow/handler.ts uses workflowId/workflowURL (workflowURL parsed by pure-string getWorkflowIdFromURL) only to select which workflow circleci.workflows.rerunWorkflow reruns via the caller's own CircleCI token; no local sink is reached.

src/tools/runPipeline/handler.ts forwards projectSlug/branch/configContent/pipelineChoiceName to CircleCI's own runPipeline API to trigger a pipeline on the caller's own project — the tool's advertised purpose; configContent is passed through as request-body data and is never parsed or executed by this server.

src/tools/runRollbackPipeline/handler.ts forwards projectSlug/projectID/environmentName/componentName/currentVersion/targetVersion/namespace/reason/parameters verbatim as the body of CircleCI's own deploys.runRollbackPipeline API call on the caller's own project/token; nothing is executed, logged into a structured file, or used as a local path.
